title: Global traffic routing overview (Route 53 and CloudFront)
hook: Amazon Route 53 routes users to healthy endpoints by DNS policy. Amazon CloudFront caches and terminates TLS at edge. Together they form the global entry layer — while your compute and data still live in Regional VPCs.

blocks.text: Route 53 is AWS DNS with routing policies: simple, weighted, latency-based, geolocation, geoproximity, and failover. Health checks remove unhealthy records. CloudFront sits in front of HTTP origins for static and dynamic content, using edge PoPs worldwide. Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs for TCP/UDP with path optimization — complementary to Route 53 and CloudFront for different layers.

blocks.text: Users experience your product through DNS and edge first. Misconfigured routing sends Mumbai users to Virginia. Failover without health checks prolongs outages. Caching APIs at CloudFront without careful TTL leaks data across users. Senior designs separate static edge delivery from Regional API with explicit policies.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: Route 53 picks Region/endpoint; CloudFront caches safe static content at edge; origins stay in VPC. Failover needs health checks and runbooks.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: User resolves DNS
items.body: Route 53 returns CloudFront domain or Regional ALB based on policy.

items.title: Edge handles cacheable traffic
items.body: CloudFront serves HIT from PoP; MISS fetches origin in Region.

items.title: API traffic to Region
items.body: /api/* behavior forwards to ALB with low or zero TTL.

items.title: Failover on outage
items.body: Health check fails primary; DNS shifts to secondary Region record.

snippet.label: Route 53 failover records
snippet.code:
PrimaryRecord:
  Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
  Properties:
    HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
    Name: api.example.com
    Type: A
    SetIdentifier: primary
    Failover: PRIMARY
    AliasTarget:
      DNSName: !GetAtt PrimaryAlb.DNSName
      HostedZoneId: !GetAtt PrimaryAlb.CanonicalHostedZoneID
    HealthCheckId: !Ref PrimaryHealthCheck
SecondaryRecord:
  Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
  Properties:
    SetIdentifier: secondary
    Failover: SECONDARY
    AliasTarget:
      DNSName: !GetAtt DrAlb.DNSName
      HostedZoneId: !GetAtt DrAlb.CanonicalHostedZoneID
snippet.explanation: Secondary serves only when primary health check fails. TTL on alias records follows AWS defaults — plan DNS propagation in runbook.

snippet.label: Create HTTP health check
snippet.explanation: Health check must reach a public endpoint or use CloudWatch alarm for private ALB patterns.

snippet.label: Latency-based routing policy test
snippet.code:
dig +short api.example.com @ns-123.awsdns-45.com
# Repeat from different geographic vantage or Route 53 Resolver
snippet.explanation: Latency policy returns different ALB aliases depending on resolver location — validate with probes, not assumption.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Failover without testing secondary Region capacity. Caching authenticated API at edge. Health check hitting private subnet without CloudWatch alarm pattern. Expecting instant DNS failover worldwide — TTL and resolver cache matter. Active-active databases without conflict strategy.

interviewTakeaways: Route 53 routing policies direct users to healthy Regional endpoints; health checks drive failover.
CloudFront caches at edge; origins remain in Regions — separate behaviors for /assets vs /api.
Multi-Region DR needs runbooks, RPO/RTO, and tested secondary capacity — DNS alone is not enough.
60s: DNS policy + health checks for Regional failover. CloudFront for static edge. API to ALB with TTL 0.
Follow-up: how do you health-check a private ALB for Route 53?
commonPitfalls: Saying CloudFront replaces multi-AZ gets you rejected — edge does not host your database.
Strong answer: name routing policy, health check, what fails over, RPO/RTO for data.
Caching /api responses with shared cache key — user A sees user B data.
DR Region cold — failover succeeds in DNS but secondary cannot handle load.
